source_search_execution_summary.stop_reason: Maximum iteration limit reached (iteration 2 of 2). All four epidemiological weeks within June 2025 (weeks 22–26) are now covered by confirmed FDOH PDF candidates. The primary remaining gap (deaths/hospitalizations) was not resolved by iteration 2 searches, and no snippet from any source confirms dengue deaths or hospitalizations in Florida during June 2025 — this is likely a true data absence rather than a retrieval gap, consistent with Florida's predominantly travel-associated dengue profile. Further searching is not possible within bounds and is unlikely to yield deaths/hospitalization data that does not exist in the public record for this period.

iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_coverage_assessment: Strong coverage of the primary target fields. FDOH weekly PDFs for weeks 22–26 provide: disease (dengue), subnational_location (Florida), locality (county-level in some reports), date_reported (epidemiological week dates), cases_confirmed/probable (FDOH tallies include confirmed and probable per its methodology note), cases_unspecified (travel-associated weekly counts), and source_url/source_type/evidence_quote. The epi.ufl.edu article provides a dated cumulative snapshot (June 14: 85 travel-associated + 1 locally acquired). The Week 42 cumulative report provides county-level breakdowns (Miami-Dade: dengue in June; Brevard: dengue in May). Deaths and hospitalizations remain unconfirmed in any retrieved snippet — no snippet from CDC, FDOH, or news sources explicitly states dengue deaths or hospitalizations for Florida in June 2025, which is consistent with the low-mortality profile of travel-associated dengue in Florida and the absence of a declared outbreak. This gap is noted but is not resolvable within the iteration limit.
iterative_source_discovery_summary.final_trustworthiness_assessment: FDOH weekly PDFs are the gold-standard authoritative source for Florida arboviral surveillance — official state health agency, .gov domain, structured surveillance program output. The epi.ufl.edu source is a credible academic public health institute that explicitly cites FDOH data. The Week 42 cumulative FDOH report provides independent corroboration of county-level dengue activity. No low-trust or unverifiable sources are being relied upon for primary case counts. The 2024-26 PDF (rank 6, iteration 2) is correctly identified as a prior-year comparator and should not be used for June 2025 data. The w6-2026 report is a future-period document and should not be used for June 2025 data.
